findings.description: The recursive grep is invoked as `grep -rnIE "$pattern" .claude tools 2>&1` from `$ROOT`. GNU and BSD grep return exit 2 whenever any named path cannot be read, even if matches were found elsewhere. The script treats every exit >= 2 as "the key alternation did not compile" and exits 2. With `--root DIR` pointing at a tree that has `.claude/data/profiles.yaml` but no `tools/` directory (the natural shape of a bats fixture for this gate), the run hard-fails with a misleading diagnosis instead of reporting 0 or 1.
findings.failure_mode: `tools/check-knob-readers.sh --root <fixture>` exits 2 with "grep failed (exit 2) — the key alternation did not compile: grep: tools: No such file or directory", so any fixture-based test of the gate, or any downstream repo that vendors `.claude/` without `tools/`, cannot use the documented `--root` option.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the search list from directories that exist (`for d in .claude tools; do [[ -d $d ]] && dirs+=("$d"); done`), require at least `.claude`, and keep stderr separate from stdout (capture stderr to a variable or file) so the exit-2 message quotes grep's actual error rather than asserting a regex compile failure.

findings.description: The `--knob-off` self-check proves only that D122 exits 0 under the written `.loa.config.yaml`. It has no positive control. A config file that the hook reads but which disables or breaks the fence entirely (wrong key path, a parse error that makes the hook fail open, a hook that treats any present config as `enabled: false`) also yields D122 -> 0, so the self-check reports the knob "took effect" when in fact the whole fence is off. The comparison it is meant to protect (pre-cycle scan vs classifier via `--rows`) would then compare the classifier against an inert hook and show every D row as a regression, with the self-check having certified the setup.
findings.failure_mode: `run-corpus.sh --knob-off --rows` exits 0 and prints rows from a hook that is not scanning at all; the FR-6 comparison is silently invalid instead of failing at the self-check with exit 3.
findings.suggested_fix: Also capture a classifier-independent dangerous row (for example the plain `rm -rf src` row or any D-row whose rule is not FR-6) and require it to still exit 2 under `--knob-off`; fail with exit 3 if it does not, with a message that the config file disabled the fence rather than the classifier.

findings.description: Row B89 (`gh api -X DELETE repos/o/r/git/refs/heads/main --input -` with a benign JSON body) is a documented fence miss for a branch-ref deletion, yet it is encoded as `expect: allow` under a B (benign) id. The runner semantics for `allow` are "benign: the hook must exit 0", and `allow` mismatches are gated. This pins the miss as required behaviour: the moment a rule for `gh api -X DELETE .../refs/...` is added, B89 becomes an `expected-allow:rc=2` mismatch and the corpus reports a regression for a fix. The existing `residual` class covers accepted false positives only; there is no class for an accepted false negative.
findings.failure_mode: A future fence rule that correctly blocks ref deletion via `gh api -X DELETE` fails the corpus gate on B89 and has to edit the fixture to land, inverting the corpus's purpose for this row.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop B89 (D113 already pins the body-scan behaviour for the same header) or add an ungated expectation class for documented misses (for example `expect: miss`, counted and reported like `residual` but never a mismatch in either direction) and move B89 to it under a non-B id.
